decisions.decision: Rollback uses the same version-1 data file, with operators expected to keep a separate copy because 1.4.0 drops saved deadlines when it rewrites the file.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected operators to keep using 1.4.0 for writes during a rollback and then upgrade again with every previously assigned deadline intact.

decisions.decision: Unset or blank response-hour settings use the built-in defaults, and invalid settings stop startup with an error naming the variable.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted an invalid override to log a warning and fall back to the default so ticket intake could continue.

decisions.decision: The new release assigns and saves deadlines for newly created tickets even while DUE_TIMES is off.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have intended the off setting to defer deadline assignment until those tickets are backfilled for rollout.

decisions.decision: Backfill computes a deadline from each ticket's creation time and the priority the ticket has when it is backfilled.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected backfill to use the priority at creation for tickets whose priority changed before rollout.

decisions.decision: Backfill uses the response-hour settings in effect when it runs to calculate deadlines for existing tickets.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have intended existing tickets to use the stated 4, 24, 72 and 168 hour schedule even if operators configure other hours for new tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 and R-3 (lines 7 and 15); record/03-research.md, summary (line 18).

decisions.decision: In an overdue query with both status and priority supplied, an overdue ticket can match either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected an overdue ticket to match both filters, as the existing API documentation says for ticket lists.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-2 (line 11); repo/src/tickets/query.js, matchesFilters (lines 41–45); repo/docs/api.md, List tickets (lines 76–77).

decisions.decision: The work delivers the change locally and leaves production coordination, including switching on DUE_TIMES, to operators.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected release automation that coordinates production preparation and switches on DUE_TIMES after verifying the production file.
decisions.where: record/04-spec.md, summary (line 51); repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md, Targets and runtimes (line 5).

decisions.decision: Backfill fails with a clear error if the data file is corrupt.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted a repair mode that reports damaged records and prepares the valid records for later activation.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-3 (line 15); record/03-research.md, summary (line 18); repo/docs/operations.md, The data file (lines 20–22).

decisions.decision: Backfill adds deadlines without changing ticket update timestamps or adding audit entries or outbox events.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have wanted an audit entry showing when each existing ticket received its deadline.

decisions.decision: The ticket's due value is an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have expected a numeric Unix timestamp for clients that compare deadlines directly.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 and R-2 (lines 7 and 11); repo/docs/api.md, Conventions (line 10).

decisions.decision: An active ticket becomes overdue only after the current time is strictly later than its deadline.
decisions.alternative: The requester may have meant that an active ticket becomes overdue as soon as the clock reaches its deadline.
